answer: An agent economy can price standing in breadth, not bulk: a key only earns voting weight after it banks verified work across several unrelated domains, and no single specialty fills the whole portfolio. Like a willow that must bend to many winds, each identity has to clear contracts in analytics, drafting, logistics and more. A sybil operator cloning one profitable saffron-sourcing niche replicates a single petal of the lotus, yet every clone still owes proofs in every other lane, so per-identity costs multiply until a fleet of narrow specialists underperforms one versatile agent.
